hints: Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane to determine the normal reaction: $R = mg \cos 20^\circ$.
Calculate the limiting friction force opposing the upward motion using $F = \mu R = 0.4(12g \cos 20^\circ)$.
Apply Newton's second law parallel to the plane: $T - F - mg \sin 20^\circ = ma$, with $m = 12\text{ kg}$ and $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Draw or visualize the free-body diagram for the block of mass $m = 12\text{ kg}$ on the rough plane inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal.

Step 1: Normal reaction force $R$.
Because there is no acceleration perpendicular to the plane, the normal reaction balances the perpendicular component of weight:
$$R = mg \cos 20^\circ = 12 \times 10 \times \cos 20^\circ = 120 \cos 20^\circ \approx 112.763\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Friction force $F$.
The block is accelerating up the plane, so friction acts down the plane opposing the motion. Because the block is moving, friction is at its maximum (limiting) value:
$$F = \mu R = 0.4(120 \cos 20^\circ) = 48 \cos 20^\circ \approx 45.105\text{ N}$$

Step 3: Component of weight along the incline.
The component of gravity acting down the slope is:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg \sin 20^\circ = 12 \times 10 \times \sin 20^\circ = 120 \sin 20^\circ \approx 41.042\text{ N}$$

Step 4: Equation of motion up the plane.
Apply Newton's second law parallel to the plane, taking the uphill direction as positive:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$T - F - mg \sin 20^\circ = ma$$
$$T - 48 \cos 20^\circ - 120 \sin 20^\circ = 12(2) = 24$$

Step 5: Solve for tension $T$:
$$T = 24 + 48 \cos 20^\circ + 120 \sin 20^\circ$$
$$T \approx 24 + 45.1053 + 41.0424 = 110.1477\text{ N} \approx 110\text{ N}$$
